title: Number of Increasing Paths in a Grid
summary: Given an m x n integer matrix grid, where you can move to any adjacent cell in all four directions, calculate the total number of distinct strictly increasing paths.
statement: Given an m x n integer matrix grid, where you can move to any adjacent cell in all four directions, calculate the total number of distinct strictly increasing paths. Paths can start and end at any cell within the grid. The result should be given modulo 10^9 + 7. Two paths are considered distinct if they do not follow the exact same sequence of cells.
constraints: A path is a nonempty sequence of cells connected by four-direction moves.
Every next cell value must be strictly greater than the previous value.
Count paths by their ordered cell sequence and return the result modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Define a recursive state as the number of increasing paths starting at one cell.
Every cell contributes its singleton path, then may extend to each strictly larger four-neighbor.
Memoize the recursive state because strictly increasing moves make the dependency graph acyclic.
Each path has a unique first step (or no step for a singleton), so the recurrence partitions paths without duplication.
editorial: Each path has a unique first step (or no step for a singleton), so the recurrence partitions paths without duplication.

tests.explanation: Four singleton paths plus four longer increasing paths give eight.
The two singleton paths and path 1-to-2 give three.
